newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq denies involvement in occupying Kurdish towns.
newsitem.headline: Iraq denies involvement in occupying Kurdish towns.

text.p: Iraq on Sunday strongly denied Kurdish rebel leader Jalal Talabani's accusation that Baghdad forces had attacked the towns of Degala and Koi Sanjaq.

"We strongly reject the statement of the agent Jalal Talabani and stress that our brave armed forces have pulled back to their previous positions completely and they have not left these positions," a spokesman for the Iraqi Culture and Information Ministry, quoted by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), said.
The Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) said Iraqi troops did help the rival Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) capture the two towns. The KDP denied it.

Senior U.S. officials have warned Iraqi President Saddam Hussein he would "pay the price" if Iraqi government forces were involved in the fighting but said they had no evidence of a direct Iraqi role in the capture of Degala and Koi Sanjaq.

"The agent Jalal al-Talabani is seeking help from his masters to fight against our Kurdish people...he also collaborated with the Iranian regime and worked for them as a guide to occupy Iraqi territory and subjected our Kurdish people to mass killing," the spokesman said.
Koi Sanjaq lies about 100 km (65 miles) northwest of Sulaimaniya, the last main PUK stronghold near the Iranian border.
